gaps.sentence: I ___ her at a conference in 2019, but we did not start working together until last year.
gaps.hint: in 2019 pins a finished past time
gaps.explanation: 'In 2019' is a finished past time, so the past simple is required: met.

gaps.sentence: The taxi ___ as soon as you come out of the terminal — look for a blue shirt.
gaps.hint: in progress at the future arrival moment
gaps.explanation: An action that will be in progress at a future moment takes the future continuous: will be waiting.

gaps.sentence: At the moment, the council ___ whether to sell the library.
gaps.hint: at the moment shows an ongoing process
gaps.explanation: 'At the moment' marks an ongoing process, so the present continuous fits: is deciding.

gaps.sentence: Don't worry about the dog — it ___ at strangers, but it never bites.
gaps.hint: typical behavior takes the present simple
gaps.explanation: Characteristic, repeated behavior takes the present simple: barks.

gaps.sentence: The village ___ a lot since the new road opened.
gaps.hint: since clause with a present result
gaps.explanation: Change that started in the past and continues to now takes the present perfect: has changed.

gaps.sentence: This jacket ___ to my brother, so please do not take it by mistake.
gaps.hint: belong is always a state verb
gaps.explanation: 'Belong' is a state verb and has no continuous form, so the present simple is correct: belongs.

gaps.hint: on the point of happening now
gaps.explanation: 'Be about to' expresses something on the point of happening: is about to start.

gaps.sentence: I ___ to contact him all week, but his phone is always engaged.
gaps.hint: all week repeated attempts until now
gaps.explanation: Repeated attempts continuing up to now take the present perfect continuous: have been trying.
